summary: This work demonstrates computations with many encoded logical qubits that outperform their unencoded counterparts using high-rate iceberg quantum error detecting and correcting codes on a trapped-ion quantum processor. Beyond-break-even performance is achieved with 48–94 logical qubits across benchmarks including state preparation, logical gates, GHZ state preparation, and partially fault-tolerant simulation of a three-dimensional $XY$ model.
motivation: High-rate codes encode many logical qubits in fewer physical qubits, reducing overhead relative to surface codes, but their implementation at beyond-classical scale has remained challenging; trapped-ion platforms with arbitrary connectivity and high-fidelity gates enable realization of these codes.
method: On the 98-qubit Quantinuum Helios trapped-ion processor with $^{137}\mathrm{Ba}^+$ qubits and Mølmer–Sørensen $U_{ZZ}(\theta)$ gates, concatenated iceberg codes $[[k+2,k,2]]$ (distance-2) and $[[(k_2+2)(k_1+2),k_2k_1,4]]$ (distance-4) were implemented with new fault-tolerant and partially fault-tolerant gadgets for initialization, syndrome extraction, and logical gates, including GHZ-based syndrome extraction with four-qubit ancillary states and a log-depth state preparation circuit.
result: SPAM infidelities per logical qubit improved by $\geq 10\times$ versus physical qubits ($3\times10^{-5}$ for distance-4 $[[80,48,4]]$); logical gate infidelities of $(1.0$–$1.2)\times10^{-4}$ outperformed bare two-qubit gate errors of $8\times10^{-4}$; GHZ state fidelities reached $\sim95\%$ in $\mathcal{I}_{94}$ codes; three-dimensional $XY$ model simulation on 64 logical qubits showed $\sim30\%$ reduction in effective two-qubit error rate ($\epsilon_{\sim 2Q} = 7.1(6)\times10^{-4}$ encoded versus $10.7(5)\times10^{-4}$ unencoded) with reasonable postselection rates.
